findings.claim: IEA June 2026 first 2027 balances: supply up ~8 mb/d to 110.3 mb/d vs demand 105.3 mb/d, implying ~5 mb/d surplus, tied to Gulf production recovery and OPEC+ higher targets
findings.source: The Logic / Argus Media: IEA cuts 2026 demand forecast, sees huge 2027 surplus
findings.excerpt: the IEA's first 2027 projections show supply surging by around 8 mb/d to 110.3 mb/d, versus expected demand of 105.3 mb/d, leaving an excess of roughly 5 mb/d

findings.claim: EIA expects 2027 global oil balance surplus of ~3.7 MMBbl/d, driven by UAE output outside OPEC quotas and softer demand
findings.source: Aegis Hedging: EIA outlook points to oversupplied oil market by 2027

findings.claim: Rystad projects non-OPEC liquids production peaks around 2027 at ~72 mb/d, then declines to just under 60 mb/d by 2040
findings.source: oilnow.gy: Rystad Energy forecast for Guyana

findings.claim: Stabroek Yellowtail/Uaru/Whiptail expected combined ~1.3 mb/d capacity by end-2027; Exxon sees 1.7 mb/d by 2030 with eight developments, Longtail under regulatory review
ExxonMobil Global Outlook: oil demand stays above 100 mb/d through 2050; argues ~15%/yr natural decline requires new investment
OPEC Sept 2026 MOMR: 2026 demand growth ~380 kb/d, 2027 growth ~2.36 mb/d to 108.19 mb/d; IEF comparison shows agencies converging on ~1.9-2.0 mb/d 2027 growth
findings.excerpt: OPEC now expects global oil demand growth to jump from just 380,000 barrels per day this year to 2.36 million bpd in 2027

note: Sources frame 2027 surplus mainly as post-Hormuz-disruption Gulf recovery; none explicitly labels structural vs cyclical. Several dates estimated; IEA July 2026 noted new Gulf attacks could upend surplus forecast.
